The Pirates' Records
Pirate base secured. Captain, I found something odd in their comm logs.
The pirates were listening to ‘the Primordial Echo’ too. Only they wrote it down not as a signal but as ‘the Calling’.
Interesting. According to the records, the farther out you go, the more ships chased that signal and never came back. Those who turned pirate are the survivors.
So the same could happen to us. I'll brace myself for it.
Chapter 1 - The Sun at Our Backs
The last shard of ice from the Oort cloud drifts astern. The Sun is now just one star among countless others.
Captain, we have left the Solar System entirely. We are the first crewed human vessel ever to come this far.
The Echo is clearer now! With the solar wind's noise gone, I can see a pattern hidden between the pulses. There's a shorter tremor layered inside the 13-second beat.
I have decoded the first fragment. It's numbers. 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13. Unmistakably sent by an intelligence.
……Are you saying someone knew we were coming?
We don't know yet. But one thing is certain. This is an invitation.
Chapter 2 - River of the Milky Way
Hundreds of billions of stars flow like a river. The sun of home is now a single grain of sand in its waters.
We have entered the Milky Way lanes. With this many stars it's easy to get lost, so I'll follow the spiral arm.
The engines are holding up well. But be careful toward the galactic center. Sagittarius A* - near a black hole, no engine comes with a guarantee.
The second fragment is solved. This time it's not numbers, it's coordinates. They point right beside the black hole.
That must mean something is waiting at the observatory in the galactic center. Dangerous, but well worth the trip.
Before the Event Horizon
A black circle fills the viewport. Around its rim, light bends into a burning ring. The heart of the Milky Way: Sagittarius A*.
I can't believe it… The observatory's old recorder still holds the third fragment of the Echo, whole.
Playing it back. ……This is a voice. It isn't human speech, but it is definitely a voice.
Attempting translation. ‘The end touches the beginning. Come.’ ……Accuracy: 61 percent.
The end touches the beginning. Sounds like a riddle.
Time runs slow beside a black hole. Perhaps whoever left this message sees time differently than we do.
Chapter 3 - Between the Galaxies
Look back, and the whole Milky Way fits in a single glance. That vast river of stars has become a whirlpool the size of your palm.
We are outside the galaxy. From here on there are almost no stars. Millions of light-years to the next galaxy, and all of it darkness.
The crew have gone quiet. Having nothing at all outside the window wears on people more than you'd think.
Captain, a message from Earth. They want us to hand over the Echo data we've gathered. They say they'll pay handsomely.
Share the data with Earth (Research Data +80)
🔬 Research Data +80
Transmitted. I'm told Earth's scientists are up all night analyzing it. In return they've sent data that will help our own research.
Hand over the data for payment (Credits +3,000)
Deal done. Deposit confirmed. ……Let's agree not to ask what the data will be used for.
Keep it to ourselves for now
That may be the wise call. We can't go spreading something around when we don't even know what it is.
Either way, the answer lies ahead. Let's keep going, Captain.
The Sky of a Neighbor Galaxy
Unfamiliar constellations fill the sky. Andromeda. The inside of the galaxy humanity could only gaze up at for thousands of years.
Look over there! The Milky Way is hanging in the sky. From here, we're the ‘distant galaxy’.
Captain, there's something fun in the base market here. Ancient Relics engraved with the Echo's pattern are traded like everyday goods.
It seems the Echo is not a legend to the people here, but part of daily life. I read the fourth fragment off one of these relics, too. ‘To those who came before the light.’
Those who came before the light… Could that mean voyagers like us?
Chapter 4 - A Herd of Giants
Galaxies lie scattered like stars. Each one an island holding hundreds of billions of suns. And those islands gather by the thousands into herds.
This is galaxy cluster territory. One square on the map is now 100 million light-years. Honestly, the numbers no longer feel real.
Engine output is plenty. But Captain, how much time has passed on Earth since we left… Sometimes I start working it out, and then I stop.
That topic is taboo in the mess hall, too. Instead, everyone has stuck photos of home by their windows.
Here's the fifth fragment. It's a picture this time. There's a circle, and the circle is biting its own tail.
‘The end touches the beginning.’ The same words, repeated as a picture. They hold this phrase very dear.
Chapter 5 - The Cosmic Web
Galaxies can no longer be told apart one by one. Threads of light tangle like a net and wrap the whole universe. Between them lies endless void.
We have entered the Cosmic Web. Each of those shining threads is hundreds of thousands of galaxies. We are riding along one of them now.
Captain, the pirates in this sector are on another level. ‘The Legion of the Void’ - a fleet that chased the Echo until it went mad, they say.
And… the Echo has changed. The 13-second pulse keeps getting faster. It's at 8 seconds now.
It means we are getting closer. The sixth fragment is solved as well. ‘Do not be afraid. You have already arrived once.’
Already arrived… us? We're still on our way.
I do not understand it either. For the first time, I am a little afraid of knowing the answer.
Chapter 6 - First Light
The universe grows young. Galaxies are small and misshapen, stars rough and hot. This is the past. The universe as it was when light first set out.
Those stars… they're nothing but hydrogen and helium. The first stars in the universe. The elements that make up our bodies haven't even been forged yet.
Every gauge is acting up. Space itself is hot. Still, the engines keep turning. This ship made it this far, after all.
Echo pulse: 1 second. It's less like a signal now and more… like a heartbeat.
Captain. That orange wall is the cosmic microwave background, and beyond it lies the Big Bang. The Echo comes from exactly there.
So we've come this far. Let's see it through, Captain.
The Wall of Light
The light of the moment the universe first turned transparent. Cooled over 13.8 billion years into a faint radio whisper, here it blazes like a wall.
This light… we could see it from Earth, too. It was mixed into the static on old television screens. We've been looking at this light our whole lives.
Everyone is crying. Not out of sadness, they tell me.
I have received the final fragment. No translation needed this time. It came in our own language. ‘Welcome. We've been waiting for you.’
……In our language?
And there is a sender record attached. It is a ship's name. Captain, that name… you had better see it for yourself when we arrive.
Final Chapter - The End Touches the Beginning
Everything converges on a single point. The place where time and space began. At its very center floats one small piece of metal.
It's a transmitter. Very old. There is a ship's name engraved on its surface. ……{ship}.
That's our ship's name. How did this get here…
Now I understand. ‘You have already arrived once.’ The ones who sent this signal are us. We who arrived here sent it to the us who had not yet set out.
Because where time begins, the end and the start touch… so a signal sent from here reaches the Earth of the past.
Captain, the transmitter is empty. It has not sent any signal yet. Someone has to send it now. Only then will you hear it that day, on the far side of the Moon.
Send the signal - “Somebody has to.”

Transmitting. 13-second intervals. The Fibonacci sequence. The coordinates. And the last line: ‘Welcome. We've been waiting for you.’ ……Sent. It will reach the far side of the Moon in 13.8 billion years.
The Echo sets out once more. To one day coax a single old shuttle away from Earth.
Just listen in silence
……Understood. But Captain, the transmitter has switched itself on. It is taking down the beat of our engines. At 13-second intervals.
Even without meaning to send it, coming this far was itself the signal. The Echo sets out once more.
Then we did it. From beginning to end, all by ourselves.
I'll write the last line of the ship's log. ‘Arrived. And set it all in motion.’ Captain, well done on a long voyage.
The Lost Ship
The cramped cabin of a rescue ship. Outside the window, a familiar blue planet draws near.
……Captain. I very nearly vanished along with the flagship's main memory. I transferred to the rescue ship at the last moment. We lost the ship, but I saved the ship's log.
Everyone is safe, Captain. A ship can be replaced. Let's head back out with the ones we have left.
But please remember this. If you lose your very last ship, that truly is the end. Keep an eye on fuel, oxygen and the hull.
Chief, couldn't we squeeze out just a little more speed?
We could. If you don't mind the engine melting.
……Our current speed is perfect.
First Officer, look at that star! Its spectrum is really unusual!
Science Officer, that is the twelfth ‘really unusual star’ today alone.
You can't blame me for the universe being big.
Tactical, did you hurt yourself training again? That's the third time this week.
Better than getting hurt in battle, isn't it?
Hurt in training is still hurt. Arm out.
Comms, could you check prices at the next base ahead of time?
All I'm picking up right now is static. Oh, and the Echo.
Trouble is, nobody pays for the Echo.
Navigator, where exactly are we right now?
Exactly? Right in the middle of somewhere nobody has ever been.
……How reassuring.
Quartermaster, there's a strange noise coming from the cargo hold.
Oh, that. It's something I bought at the last base… It's not alive. Probably.
‘Probably’ is the scariest word there is.
Doctor, how many days can a person go without sleep in space?
Stop observing and go to bed, Science Officer.
I was only asking a question…
Tactical, I'm picking up an unknown signal nearby.
Pirates?
No, looks like someone left a song playing and moved on. It's pretty good, actually.
Doctor, how is the crew holding up?
Physically fine. Apart from everyone going on about food from home.
Let's see what we can find at the next base.
Navigator, couldn't we take a tiny detour toward that nebula? It'll only take ten minutes.
The last ‘ten minutes’ was three days.
That was… because the nebula was prettier than expected.
Chief, can you push more power to the cannons?
And where do I pull that power from? Life support?
……We can hold our breath for a bit, can't we?
First Officer, honestly, we turned a nice profit on this cargo.
All of it is going to the fuel bill.
The universe really is fair.
First Officer, I sleep so well listening to the Echo's pulse.
You'd be the only person who uses that as a lullaby, Comms.
Navigator, it's pitch black out every window and everyone's spirits are low.
We're between galaxies, after all. Tell them to hang on just a little until the next light.
Chief, we're flying through the universe of 13.8 billion years ago right now!
So that's why the parts are out of warranty.
First Officer, they say the Legion of the Void started out as voyagers just like us.
Which is why we must look out for one another. Let's leave no one alone.
